items.name: Cardiogen
items.benefits: Cardiogen is described as a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg / AEDR) proposed for cardiac tissue research. The source summarizes preclinical findings in cultured rat myocardial tissue, mouse fibroblasts, and a rat sarcoma model. These findings do not establish benefit, safety, or effective dosing in people; the source states that no human clinical trials have established an optimal dose.

protocols.title: Cardiogen — Pep-Pedia community-derived reference
protocols.population: Unspecified; the source identifies these doses as community-derived and says human clinical trials have not established optimal dosing.
protocols.evidenceNotes: Pep-Pedia labels the injectable protocols community-derived. It states that preclinical studies used in vitro concentrations, not injectable human doses. Its 10–20 mg every 3–7 days schedule differs substantially from the 200–500 mcg daily schedule on Dosage Peptide; the sources are kept separate and neither is evidence of a safe or effective human regimen.

schedule.description: Every 3–7 days; source-described as community-derived, not clinically established.

source_statements.excerpt: Injectable dosing protocols are community-derived. No human clinical trials have established optimal dosing for Cardiogen. All preclinical studies used in vitro concentrations (ng/ml range), not injectable human doses.
Not recommended during active cancer due to proliferative effects on fibroblasts
Contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation due to absence of safety data

regimen.notes: Source reference only. The source describes 2–4 week cycles and a 3–6 month break between cycles; the schedule remains unverified as human dosing.

protocols.title: Cardiogen — Dosage Peptide source daily titration (unverified)
protocols.population: Unspecified; the source identifies this as research-only information and says the schedule is not approved human dosing.
protocols.evidenceNotes: Commercial secondary source; independent verification is pending. This source's 200–500 mcg daily titration conflicts substantially with Pep-Pedia's 10–20 mg every 3–7 days community-derived schedule. Within this page, the narrative says to increase by about 100 mcg every two weeks, while the table advances from 400 mcg for Week 5 to 500 mcg for Weeks 6–12. The differences are preserved rather than reconciled; neither schedule is established for human use.

provenance.locator: Dosing & Reconstitution Guide; Standard / Gradual Approach

storage.notes: The source reports storing lyophilized vials at −20 °C (−4 °F), and refrigerating reconstituted solution at 2–8 °C (35.6–46.4 °F), protected from light, without freezing. It says to use the mixed solution within about 28 days.

source_statements.excerpt: All information on DosagePeptide.com is for research and educational purposes only. Research compounds referenced here are intended for laboratory and research use only — not for human consumption — and are not FDA-approved for human use.

there are no high-quality independent human randomized trials of Cardiogen. The cardioprotective, “genetic-repair” and rejuvenation claims associated with the Khavinson bioregulators rest on the originators’ preclinical work and should be read as unproven hypotheses, not established benefits.
Increase by roughly 100 mcg every two weeks as tolerated.

regimen.notes: Source reference only. The page describes 8–12 weeks as typical, with some references extending to about 16 weeks. Its detailed table covers 12 weeks, and its every-two-weeks titration note does not exactly match the Week 5 to Weeks 6–12 table transition.
